newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Telewest says not in merger talks.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Telewest says not in merger talks.

text.p: Telewest Communications, presently Britain's biggest cable television and telephone operator, said on Wednesday that it was not in merger talks but thought consolidation "a very good move for the industry".

Telewest's chief financial officer Charles Burdick told Reuters he welcomed news that four cable companies -- Cable and Wireless's Mercury unit, British cable company Videotron, Bell Cablemedia and NYNEX CableComms -- were planning to complete their merger this spring. "A more fragmented industry makes it harder to co-operate," he said.

"We see the industry ripe for consolidation because of the cost structure that is cheaper to spread over a larger base...as we get issues like branding, national advertising, rolling out digital," he added.
But Burdick declined to comment on newspaper reports that Telewest had been in merger talks at different times with both General Cable and NYNEX CableComms.
"We cant comment but there are no discussions going on," he said.

Newspapers have said that merger talks with NYNEX CableComms, aimed at creating a diminant UK cable company more able to competed with satellite broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting, broke off last October after more than a year of on-off negotiations with Telewest.
But since then, NYNEX CableComms, controlled by America's NYNEX Corp, has found a new ally in the form of Cable and Wireless's new cable company.
The group will be called Cable and Wireless Communications and will be Britain's biggest cable company.
